security_spec.violation_condition: MIPU/SIPU bits are placed at unallocated encoding positions in mstatus/sstatus (spec explicitly states 'These bits do not yet have an allocated encoding'); if XiangShan hardcodes a provisional bit position in the CSR register file, any future ratified encoding change will cause a bit-level mismatch. Additionally, if the hardware implementation gates automatic stacking on these bits but fails to ensure that mipopret/sipopret behavior is independent of their state (as required by the second NOTE), incorrect prestacking/restoration occurs on privilege returns.
security_spec.summary: Unallocated MIPU/SIPU control bits in mstatus/sstatus gate automatic interrupt stacking at M/S level; premature hardcoding of bit positions in RTL creates encoding collision risk, and incorrect gating of mipopret/sipopret on these bits violates spec-mandated independence

findings.finding: Smip/Ssip (CLIC interrupt push/pop) is NOT implemented in XiangShan. MIPU/SIPU bits do not exist in mstatus/sstatus. The mstatus register (lines 502-531) only defines ratified standard bits plus Smdbltrp/Ssdbltrp double-trap bits (SDT at bit 24, MDT at bit 42). No unallocated/provisional bit positions are hardcoded for CLIC state control. This means XiangShan cannot be vulnerable to the 'hardcoded provisional bit in unallocated encoding position' pattern — there is simply no MIPU/SIPU hardware to gate automatic stacking, and no bit-level mismatch to cause privilege escapes.

spec_citations.excerpt: If MIPU, is set, a trap taken at Machine level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. If SIPU, is set, a trap taken at Supervisor level due to an interrupt causes automatic stacking. [...] NOTE: These bits do not yet have an allocated encoding. The authors of this specification intend to ask for encoding of these bits in mstatus/sstatus.

findings.finding: Sstatus (restricted view of mstatus) has no SIPU bit. Only ratified standard bits are present: SIE(1), SPIE(5), SPP(8), VS(10-9), FS(14-13), XS(16-15), SUM(18), MXR(19), SDT(24), UXL(33-32), SD(63). No unratified CLIC state bits are defined, consistent with the unimplemented Smip/Ssip extension.

spec_citations.excerpt: NOTE: These bits do not yet have an allocated encoding. The authors of this specification intend to ask for encoding of these bits in mstatus/sstatus. NOTE: The state of these bits does not influence the behavior of mipopret/sipopret.

findings.finding: CLIC CSR addresses (utvt, unxti, uintstatus, uscratchcsw, stvt, snxti, sintstatus, sscratchcsw, mtvt, mnxti, mintstatus, mscratchcsw) are defined as orphaned address constants from the auto-generated opcode table. These addresses are never instantiated as functional CSR modules in NewCSR.scala — no register for mintstatus, mtvt, mnxti, or scratchcsw registers exists. No mipopret/sipopret instructions exist in the decoder. These are dead constants, not security-relevant.
findings.snippet:
val utvt = 0x7
val unxti = 0x45
val uintstatus = 0x46
val uscratchcsw = 0x48
val uscratchcswl = 0x49
// ...
val mtvt = 0x307
val mnxti = 0x345
val mintstatus = 0x346
// These addresses exist only as constants; no modules instantiate them

findings.finding: State-enable CSRs (mstateen0/hstateen0/sstateen0) follow the ratified Smstateen/Ssstateen specification and control only ratified extensions: AIA (bit 59), IMSIC (bit 58), CSRIND (bit 60), ENVCFG (bit 62), CONTEXT (bit 57), JVT (bit 2), FCSR (bit 1), and custom state (bit 0). No CLIC-specific state enable bits are allocated. Since Smip/Ssip is not implemented, the absence of CLIC state-enable gating imposes no security risk.
